In [[mathematical logic]], '''Gödel logics''', sometimes referred to as '''Dummett logics''' or '''Gödel–Dummett logics''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=von Plato |first=Jan |date=2003 |title=Skolem's Discovery of Gödel-Dummett Logic|url=http://link.springer.com/10.1023/A:1022997524909 |journal=[[Studia Logica]] |volume=73 |issue=1 |pages=153–157 |doi=10.1023/A:1022997524909|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a family of [[finite-valued logic|finite-]] or [[infinite-valued logic]]s in which the sets of [[truth value]]s ''V'' are [[closed subset]]s of the [[unit interval]] [0,1] containing both 0 and 1. Different such sets ''V'' in general determine different Gödel logics.

Gödel logics have several alternative definitions. Specifically, Gödel logics are:

* logics of linearly-ordered [[Heyting algebra|Heyting algebras]]<ref name=":1">{{cite book |last1=Preining |first1=Norbert |title=Logic for Programming, Artificial Intelligence, and Reasoning |chapter=Gödel Logics – A Survey |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |date=2010 |volume=6397 |pages=30–51 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-16242-8_4 |isbn=978-3-642-16241-1 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-642-16242-8_4 |access-date=2 March 2022}}</ref>
* logics of (classes of) linearly ordered and countable intuitionistic Kripke structures with constant domains<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beckmann |first1=Arnold |last2=Preining |first2=Norbert |date=March 2007 |title=Linear Kripke frames and Gödel logics |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-symbolic-logic/article/abs/linear-kripke-frames-and-godel-logics/A73924FD06586954DBF42AC4DFACBFD1 |journal=The Journal of Symbolic Logic |language=en |volume=72 |issue=1 |pages=26–44 |doi=10.2178/jsl/1174668382 |issn=0022-4812|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* logics of relative comparison, in contrast to [[Łukasiewicz logic]], which is a logic of absolute comparison or metric comparison

The concept is named after [[Kurt Gödel]] and [[Michael Dummett]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Baaz |first1=Matthias |last2=Preining |first2=Norbert |last3=Zach |first3=Richard |date=2007-06-01 |title=First-order Gödel logics |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S016800720700019X |journal=[[Annals of Pure and Applied Logic]] |volume=147 |issue=1 |pages=23–47 |doi=10.1016/j.apal.2007.03.001 |issn=0168-0072|arxiv=math/0601147 }}</ref><ref name=":1" />

== Semantics ==

=== Propositional ===
Given a propositional Gödel logic, an interpretation of it is defined as follows:

* Each propositional variable <math>p</math> is assigned a truth value <math>I[p] \in V</math>.
* <math>I[A \or B] = \max (I[A], I[B])</math>.
* <math>I[A \and B] = \min (I[A], I[B])</math>.
* <math>I[A \to B] = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{ if } I[A] \leq I[B],\\
I[B] & \text{ if } I[A] > I[B]
\end{cases}</math>
* <math>I[\bot] = 0</math>
* <math>I [\neg A] := I[A \to \bot] = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{ if } I[A] = 0,\\
0 & \text{ else.}
\end{cases}</math>
* <math>I [\top] := I[\neg\bot] := I[\bot \to \bot] = 1
 </math>
For this logic, there is usually also another unary logical connective <math>\Delta</math>, such that a model of it must satisfy<math display="block">I(\Delta A) = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{ if } I[A] = 1,\\
0 & \text{ else.}
\end{cases}</math>and a binary logical connective <math>\prec
 </math> defined by <math>A\prec B := (B \to A) \to B</math>, which implies<math display="block">I[A \prec B] = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{ if } I[A] < I[B],\\
I[B] & \text{ if } I[A] \geq I[B]
\end{cases}</math>Note that for this, we do not need <math>V</math> to be a closed set, only that <math>V</math> contain <math>0, 1</math>.

=== First-order ===
Given a first-order logic, it corresponds to a first-order Gödel logic. An interpretation of it is defined essentially the same as the first-order logic:

* There is a nonempty set <math>M</math>, the universe of the interpretation.
* For each variable symbol <math>v</math>, there is an element <math>v^I \in M</math>.
* For each ''k''-ary function symbol <math>f</math>, there is a function <math>f^I: M^k \to M</math>.
* For each ''k''-ary relation symbol <math>R</math>, there is a function <math>R^I: M^k \to V</math>.
* For each term <math>f(t_1, \dots, t_k)</math>, its interpretation is <math>f(t_1, \dots, t_k)^I := f^I(t_1^I , \dots, t_k^I)</math>.
* For each atomic formula <math>R(t_1, \dots, t_k)</math>, its interpreted truth value is <math>I(R(t_1, \dots, t_k)) := R^I(t_1^I , \dots, t_k^I)</math>.
* The propositional logic connectives works the same as before. 
* For each <math>\forall x, A</math>, its interpreted truth value is <math>I(\forall x, A) := \inf_{m \in M} I[m/x] (A) </math>, where <math>I[m/x]</math> is defined as the interpretation generated by setting <math>x^I </math> to <math>m</math> instead.
* For each <math>\exists x, A</math>, its interpreted truth value is <math>I(\exists x, A) := \sup_{m \in M} I[m/x] (A) </math>,

Note that for this, we do need <math>V</math> to be a closed set, since otherwise the quantified formulas is not guaranteed to have a truth value.

=== Entailment ===
For any set <math>\Gamma</math> of formulas, and any interpretation <math>I</math>, define <math>I(\Gamma) := \inf_{A \in \Gamma} I(A)</math>, with the special case that <math>I(\emptyset) = 1</math>.

We say that <math>\Gamma \models_V A</math> iff for any interpretation <math>I</math> into <math>V</math>, <math>I(\Gamma) \leq I(A)</math>. In particular, <math> \models_V A</math> iff for any interpretation <math>I</math> into <math>V</math>, <math>I(A) = 1</math>.

== Syntax ==
In 1959, [[Michael Dummett]] showed that infinite-valued [[propositional logic|propositional]] Gödel logic can be axiomatised by adding the [[axiom schema]]
:<math>(A \rightarrow B) \lor (B \rightarrow A)</math>
to [[Intuitionistic propositional calculus|intuitionistic propositional logic]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dummett |first=Michael |date=1959 |title=A propositional calculus with denumerable matrix |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-symbolic-logic/article/abs/propositional-calculus-with-denumerable-matrix/732272974D4555B251B046732D2708BC |journal=[[The Journal of Symbolic Logic]] |language=en |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=97–106 |doi=10.2307/2964753 |jstor=2964753 |issn=0022-4812|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
